bestFor: Verifying a Polish counterparty
Confirming REGON, NIP or KRS identifiers

Businesses not registered in Poland
pros: Free public access and an API
Publication on the site confirms the registration entry

editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. Operated by Główny Urząd Statystyczny.

name: Centralna Ewidencja i Informacja o Działalności Gospodarczej
description: Polish register of sole traders and the self-employed, supervised by the Ministry of Development and Technology, offering a free public search that returns entrepreneur records and downloadable certificates.
nativeName: Centralna Ewidencja i Informacja o Działalności Gospodarczej
englishName: Central Registration and Information on Economic Activity

operator.name: Ministry of Development and Technology (supervising authority)

publicAccess.notes: Record states: free public search that issues downloadable certificates. The overall access posture is not established, so the level stays unknown.

bestFor: Registering as a sole trader in Poland
Checking whether a Polish sole trader is currently registered
notRecommendedFor: Companies that must register in the KRS instead
Marketing exposure
pros: Free public search that issues downloadable certificates
The statutory route through which Polish sole traders come into existence
cons: Covers sole traders only; companies register in the KRS
The register interface is published in Polish
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. www.ceidg.gov.pl returns a 302 to aplikacja.ceidg.gov.pl, which states the portal is "supervised by the Ministry of Development and Technology". biznes.gov.pl, the official government business portal, gives the English name "Central Registration and Information on Economic Activity" and states that sole traders register in CEIDG while companies register in the KRS. The public search is at https://www.ceidg.gov.pl/CEIDG/CEIDG.Public.UI/Search.aspx

name: Krajowy Rejestr Sądowy
description: Krajowy Rejestr Sądowy is the Polish National Court Register, kept by the registry courts under the Act of 20 August 1997. It comprises the register of entrepreneurs — commercial companies, cooperatives, state enterprises and branches of foreign entrepreneurs — together with the register of associations, other social and professional organisations, foundations and public healthcare institutions.

publicAccess.notes: The web search interface refused automated requests behind a bot-protection interstitial and its behaviour was not observed. Free anonymous access was instead confirmed against the ministry’s own open API at api-krs.ms.gov.pl, which returned a complete current extract for a test entity without any credential.

bestFor: Confirming that a Polish company, cooperative, association or foundation legally exists and reading its recorded officers and representation.
Obtaining a current extract for a Polish registered entity by its KRS number.
notRecommendedFor: Checking a Polish sole trader, who is not in this register at all but in CEIDG.
Treating an entry as evidence of solvency, creditworthiness or good standing, none of which the register records.
recommendedIndustries: Entities registered in the Polish National Court Register
pros: It is the constitutive register for Polish companies, cooperatives, associations and foundations, so an entry establishes legal existence rather than merely describing a business.
The Ministry of Justice publishes a free open API that returns a complete current extract for an entity without any account, which makes verification reproducible rather than screen-dependent.
One register covers both the commercial sector and the association and foundation sector, through two separate statutory sub-registers.
Financial documents filed by registered entities are held in the associated document repository, so filings can be reached from the register entry.
cons: It does not cover sole traders. A Polish natural person trading on their own account is registered in CEIDG, and neither register contains the other’s population.

The NIP and REGON numbers shown in a KRS extract originate in the tax register and in the REGON statistical register and are placed in KRS automatically; they are not established by the registry court.
The public web search sits behind bot protection that refused automated requests, so its interactive behaviour, any fee for certified output and any CAPTCHA could not be observed.
An entry records legal existence and filed data. It is not a statement about solvency, creditworthiness or the conduct of the entity.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from official Polish sources: the consolidated text of the Act of 20 August 1997 on the National Court Register fetched from the Sejm’s official ELI service, the Ministry of Justice pages on gov.pl, and the ministry’s open KRS API. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The register is constituted by ustawa z dnia 20 sierpnia 1997 r. o Krajowym Rejestrze Sądowym and is kept by the registry courts (sądy rejonowe holding the KRS commercial divisions); entries are made by those courts. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Minister Sprawiedliwości, who under the Act provides the ICT system through which the register operates and through which filings are made. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately identified. No official page fetched names an external consortium or contractor for the Polish court-register systems, unlike Italy or Spain, so no technical provider is asserted. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public search at wyszukiwarka-krs.ms.gov.pl, alongside the Portal Rejestrów Sądowych and the open API at api-krs.ms.gov.pl. Relationships, all statutory rather than inferred: KRS Act art. 20 ust. 1c transmits entry data to the REGON national official register of business entities; art. 20 ust. 1a places the NIP and REGON numbers in KRS automatically after transmission from the tax register and from REGON, so those identifiers originate elsewhere. The CEIDG Act art. 2 ust. 2 pkt 1 defines CEIDG’s task as recording entrepreneurs who are natural persons, which is a population disjoint from the KRS register of entrepreneurs. Registry types: company-register for the constitutive function over companies, business-entity-register because the Act’s sub-registers span cooperatives, associations, foundations and healthcare institutions as well, and public-filing-database for the financial documents repository. cross-border-registry-interface was considered and rejected: participation in the European register interconnection does not make a national constitutive register an interface.

name: Krajowy Rejestr Zadłużonych
description: Krajowy Rejestr Zadłużonych is the Polish register of debtors, kept by the Minister of Justice under the Act of 6 December 2018. It discloses restructuring and bankruptcy proceedings, proceedings on a ban from conducting business activity, enforcement discontinued as ineffective, and maintenance arrears older than three months.

publicAccess.notes: The access position could not be observed. Every request to the portal, including with full browser headers, returned an Imperva/Incapsula interstitial rather than the application, and unlike the National Court Register there is no sibling open API to verify against. The Act states that the register is public and that everyone may consult its data over the internet, but that is the legal position rather than an observed behaviour, so no search URL is published and every access boolean stays null.

bestFor: Checking whether a Polish person or entity is subject to restructuring, bankruptcy or secondary insolvency proceedings.
Finding whether enforcement against a Polish debtor was discontinued because it would not recover more than the cost of enforcing.
notRecommendedFor: Confirming that a Polish company exists or reading its officers, which is the National Court Register rather than this register.
Treating an absence of entries as evidence of solvency. The register records proceedings that have been opened, not a financial assessment.
recommendedIndustries: Parties to Polish insolvency, restructuring and enforcement proceedings
pros: It is a single statutory register for insolvency, restructuring, ineffective enforcement and maintenance arrears, populations that are otherwise spread across separate court and enforcement files.
The Act designates it as the Polish insolvency register for the purposes of the European insolvency regulation, so it is the register other member states connect to.

The Ministry of Justice publishes its scope and legal basis on its own pages, so what the register does and does not disclose can be checked against the responsible authority rather than a commentary.
cons: The portal is behind bot protection that returned an Imperva interstitial to every request, so no search behaviour, fee or credential requirement could be observed and none is asserted here.
There is no open API alongside the portal, unlike the National Court Register, so the access position cannot be established indirectly either.
Entries describe proceedings and enforcement outcomes. They are not a credit assessment and do not establish that a debt is currently owed.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from official Polish sources: the Ministry of Justice page for the register on gov.pl, and the text of the Act of 6 December 2018 on the National Register of Debtors fetched from the Sejm’s official ELI service. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The register is constituted by ustawa z dnia 6 grudnia 2018 r. o Krajowym Rejestrze Zadłużonych and is kept by the Minister of Justice in an ICT system. Its content originates with the insolvency and restructuring courts and with enforcement bodies — court enforcement officers, tax office heads and social insurance branch directors — which post the entries the Act assigns to them. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Minister Sprawiedliwości. The ministry’s own page describes the register as a public register kept by the Minister of Justice. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not established. No official page fetched names a supplier for the portal application; the host sits behind an Imperva/Incapsula edge, which is a protection layer rather than a disclosed platform operator. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public portal at krz.ms.gov.pl. The ministry’s guidance also describes a second front door at prs.ms.gov.pl, which was not exercised here. Relationships: this register is distinct from the National Court Register, which constitutes companies; the KRS number appears here only as an identifier and a search key. Registry types: insolvency-register because the Act’s core population is restructuring and bankruptcy proceedings, and public-filing-database because the Act also provides for announcements to be made in the register. exclusion-and-debarment-register was considered, because the register discloses proceedings on a ban from conducting business activity, and rejected: that type is for a register whose subject matter is the exclusion itself, and the boundary note excludes court proceedings databases. Access: nothing was observed. An earlier pass held this record back for exactly that reason; it is published now because identity, authority, scope and legal basis are all evidenced, with the access position recorded as unknown rather than guessed — the same treatment already applied to the French national business register.

name: KNF Wyszukiwarka podmiotów
description: The Polish Financial Supervision Authority publishes a search over the entities it supervises, with category filters and an option to include entities that have been struck off. The authority states on the search page itself that it does not cover every register it keeps.

publicAccess.notes: The search form was served directly and anonymously, including its category selector and the option to include struck-off entities, but no query was executed, so no result behaviour is asserted and no search URL is published.

bestFor: Checking whether a financial entity is supervised in Poland, including entities that have since been struck off.
Reaching the Polish supervisor’s own record rather than a commercial reproduction of it.
notRecommendedFor: Treating a nil result as proof that an entity is unsupervised. The authority states that some of its registers are not covered by this search.
Company verification, which is the National Court Register rather than a supervisory search.
pros: It is the supervisor’s own search, covering supervised entities across categories in one place.
It can include entities that have been struck off, so a historical check is possible rather than only a current-status one.
The authority states the search’s own limits on the search page, rather than leaving a user to assume completeness.
cons: It is explicitly incomplete. The authority directs users to check registers that this search does not include, so absence here is not absence from supervision.
No query was executed during verification, so result content, export and any rate limit are unestablished.
Supervision is not endorsement. An entry says an entity is supervised, not that it is solvent or well conducted.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by direct fetch of the search page, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The supervisory and authorisation decisions of the Polish Financial Supervision Authority, taken under Polish financial supervision law. The search publishes those; it does not constitute them. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Komisja Nadzoru Finansowego. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately established. No external supplier is named on any page fetched. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The entity search on the authority’s own site. Completeness, carried into the published text rather than left in these notes: the search page itself tells a user that if the information sought is not found, they should also check registers that are not included in the search engine. That caveat is the single most important thing a reader needs about this system, and the record states it in the cons and in what it is not recommended for. The record deliberately does NOT claim the search covers every register the authority keeps.

name: Lista radców prawnych
description: The national list of Polish legal advisers (radcowie prawni), published by the National Chamber of Legal Advisers over the lists kept by the nineteen regional chambers. It records entry on the list and shows whether a person is currently practising, which is a separate question from being entered.

publicAccess.notes: Result rows were rendered to an anonymous client with no credential and no payment, showing surname, forename, entry number and regional chamber, and the page reported 57,288 results at the time of verification. Free public reading is therefore observed rather than inferred. Filters offered for surname, entry number, district, city and practising status. No filtered query was submitted, so behaviour under a specific search and any rate limit were not observed and stay null.

bestFor: Checking whether a named person is entered on the Polish list of legal advisers.
Establishing which regional chamber a legal adviser belongs to.
notRecommendedFor: Checking a Polish advocate. Adwokaci are a separate profession with a separate register and do not appear here.
Assuming every entry is currently practising. The list marks practising and non-practising members alike.
pros: Results are readable without an account or payment, which makes it directly usable for verification.
It states the regional chamber for each entry, across all nineteen chambers from Białystok to Zielona Góra.
It exposes practising status as a filter, so a reader can distinguish an entered person from a practising one.
cons: Entry on the list is required to practise as a legal adviser, so this is a licence register — but an entry is not a statement about competence in any field of law.
The list includes members who do not practise. A hit alone does not establish that a person is currently providing legal services, and reading it that way is the most likely error.
Polish advocates (adwokaci) are a different profession with their own register. Absence here does not establish that a person may not act as a lawyer in Poland.
Trainees and foreign lawyers are kept on separate lists by the same chamber, so this search does not cover them.
The chamber publishes the national list, but the underlying lists are kept by the nineteen regional chambers, so entries reflect regional decisions.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by direct fetch of the chamber’s national search, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The page is server-rendered and returned result rows to an anonymous client, reporting "57288 wyników" on both passes. It offers filters for "Wyszukiwanie po nazwisku", "Wyszukiwanie po nr wpisu", "Okręg", "Miasto" and "Status", the status values being "Wykonuje zawód" and "Nie wykonuje zawodu". Nineteen regional chambers are selectable: OIRP Białystok, Bydgoszcz, Gdańsk, Katowice, Kielce, Koszalin, Kraków, Lublin, Łódź, Opole, Olsztyn, Poznań, Rzeszów, Szczecin, Toruń, Wałbrzych, Warszawa, Wrocław, Zielona Góra. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The lists of legal advisers kept by the nineteen regional chambers (okręgowe izby radców prawnych); the national chamber publishes the aggregate. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Krajowa Izba Radców Prawnych, a public-law professional self-government body. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately established. Served from the chamber’s own kirp.pl domain. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The national list search at kirp.pl. Separation decisions: the chamber also publishes a list of trainees ("Lista aplikantów radcowskich") and a list of foreign lawyers ("Lista prawników zagranicznych") on separate pages. Those are distinct populations and are NOT merged into this record. Two further chamber lists — representatives before the European Court of Human Rights and advisers supporting victims of human trafficking — are thematic sign-up lists rather than registers of entitlement and were rejected as candidates.

name: Rejestr biegłych rewidentów
description: The Polish register of statutory auditors, kept by the National Council of Statutory Auditors. It records individual auditors entitled to carry out statutory audits; audit firms are kept on a separate list by the same chamber.

publicAccess.notes: Result rows were rendered to an anonymous client with no credential and no payment, showing register number and name, and the page reported 4,811 entries at the time of verification. Free public reading is therefore observed rather than inferred. Search fields offered for surname or number and for an associated audit firm. No filtered query was submitted, so behaviour under a specific search and any rate limit were not observed and stay null.

bestFor: Checking that a named person is entered in the Polish register of statutory auditors.
Establishing which audit firm an auditor is associated with.
notRecommendedFor: Checking an audit firm. Firms are kept on a separate list and do not appear in this register.
Judging audit quality. The register records entitlement, not how any engagement was performed.
pros: The register states its own keeper on the page: it is kept by the National Council of Statutory Auditors.
Results are readable without an account or payment, with the register number shown beside each name.
It can be searched by an associated audit firm as well as by name, which links a person to the practice they work in.
cons: Entry is required to carry out statutory audits, so this is a licence register — but it says nothing about the quality of any audit.
It records individual auditors only. Audit firms are kept on a separate list by the same chamber, so absence here does not establish that a firm may not audit.
The chamber keeps the register and admits its members; that is not the same as supervising an individual engagement.
The published entry point carries a query parameter that selects the auditors view, so a link stripped of it may not land on this register.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by navigating from the chamber’s own site, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The page states: "Rejestr biegłych rewidentów prowadzony jest przez Krajową Radę Biegłych Rewidentów." It is server-rendered and returned rows to an anonymous client, reporting "Znaleziono: 4811" on both passes. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The register of statutory auditors kept by the Krajowa Rada Biegłych Rewidentów, the chamber’s national council. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Polska Izba Biegłych Rewidentów, a public-law professional self-government body. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately established. Served from the chamber’s own pibr.org.pl domain. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public register search at pibr.org.pl. Separation decision: the chamber also publishes a "Lista firm audytorskich" as a separate menu item and a separate population. It was NOT merged into this record and was NOT published in this wave, because its keeper and statutory basis were not established to publication standard — Polish audit oversight was restructured in 2020 and the question of which body keeps the firm list must be settled from official text before it is recorded.

name: Lista doradców podatkowych
description: The official list of Polish tax advisers, published by the National Chamber of Tax Advisers. Entry on the list is a statutory condition of performing tax advisory activities, and performing them without entitlement is punishable by a fine.

publicAccess.notes: The search form was served anonymously with no credential, with fields for surname, forename, entry number, region and keyword, so login is recorded as not required. Submitting the form requires acknowledging the privacy policy, and no query was executed, so result content and any limits were not observed and stay null.

bestFor: Checking that a person holding themselves out as a Polish tax adviser holds the required entitlement.
Confirming an adviser’s entry number before instructing them.
notRecommendedFor: Finding an adviser by specialism. The list records entitlement, not expertise.
Checking an entitled company. Entities authorised to perform tax advisory activities are published separately.
pros: The chamber describes it as the official and continuously updated list of tax advisers.
It states the legal consequence plainly: holding an entry number on the list is the condition of performing tax advisory activities.
It warns that performing tax advisory activities without entitlement is punishable by a fine of up to 50,000 złoty under Article 81 of the Tax Advisory Act of 5 July 1996.
It can be narrowed to any of the sixteen regional chambers.
cons: Entry is required to perform tax advisory activities, so this is a licence register — but it is not a statement about how any engagement was carried out.
The search cannot be submitted without acknowledging the privacy policy, so reading the list is not a single anonymous click.
The chamber publishes a separate register of entitled entities as a downloadable PDF rather than a searchable register, so a company cannot be checked here.
Absence does not establish that a person may not act at all in tax matters; it establishes that they are not entered on this list of tax advisers.
No search was executed during verification, so result content and any limits were not observed and none is asserted.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by navigating from the chamber’s own site, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The page states it is the "Oficjalna i na bieżąco aktualizowana lista doradców podatkowych", that a reader can check "czy osoba podająca się za doradcę podatkowego posiada wymagane prawem uprawnienia do wykonywania tego zawodu", and that "Warunkiem wykonywania czynności doradztwa podatkowego jest posiadanie numeru wpisu na listę." It warns: "Kto, nie będąc uprawniony, wykonuje czynności doradztwa podatkowego, podlega grzywnie do 50 000 zł", citing "Art. 81 ustawy z dnia 5 lipca 1996 r. o doradztwie podatkowym". Sixteen regional chambers are selectable. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: Entry on the list of tax advisers under the Tax Advisory Act of 5 July 1996; the chamber enters and publishes. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Krajowa Izba Doradców Podatkowych, a public-law professional self-government body. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately established. Served from the chamber’s own kidp.pl domain. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public list search at kidp.pl, behind a privacy-policy acknowledgement. Rejected as a separate record: the chamber’s "Rejestr podmiotów uprawnionych" is published as a static PDF download, not a searchable register, and is recorded here as a limitation of this record rather than as a system of its own.

name: Panorama Firm
description: A Polish business directory in the WeNet group. Adding a company is free, and the form offers two distinct routes — one for the business owner and one for a customer adding a company they used — so entries do not all originate with the business they name.
bestFor: Polish businesses wanting a free national directory entry.
Adding a Polish local citation quickly, without an account.
notRecommendedFor: Businesses that need control over who created their entry. A customer can add a company they used.
Anyone treating an entry as verified data. Nothing about verification is documented.
pros: Adding a company is free and stated as such: “Dodaj firmę bezpłatnie”.
The operator describes what the business gets in return — “darmową wizytówkę swojego biznesu w Internecie” — rather than leaving the offer vague.
Profiles carry opinions, so the directory supports reputation as well as lookup.
The submission route is a plain form at a stable address.
cons: The submission form asks whether you are the owner or a user — “Jestem: Właścicielem / Użytkownikiem” — so a third party who used a business can add it. An entry is not evidence that the named business created or approved it.
Creating an entry is confirmed; claiming an existing third-party entry is not documented, so no claim flow is asserted.
Nothing about verification is documented, so it is not asserted. Combined with third-party submission, entry data should be treated as unverified.
Opinions appear on profiles, but whether a business can respond to them is not documented and is not asserted.
The operating company is identified only through footer links to WeNet properties rather than a naming statement on the directory itself.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 from the directory and its own submission form, and re-verified in a separate direct pass in which “Dodaj firmę bezpłatnie”, “Właścicielem” and “darmową wizytówkę” were each present in the served pages. PLATFORM OPERATOR: WeNet. The directory footer links to wenet.pl properties and a WeNet Club; the group is not named in a statement on the directory itself, which is why the operator is recorded under the group brand rather than a specific company. LISTING CONTROL: Either the business owner or a customer may add a company, which the form asks explicitly. MODERATION AUTHORITY: Not documented by the operator. PUBLIC INTERFACE: panoramafirm.pl, with the submission form at /dodaj-firme.html. DUPLICATE DECISION: kept separate from pkt.pl even though both sit in the WeNet group. Ownership is not evidence of one system: the two run different submission forms on different domains, pkt.pl carries its own site terms, and neither states that a submission reaches the other. Shared group ownership is disclosed in prose instead. NOT ASSERTED: verification, owner responses, claim flow, indexability, link attributes, traffic.

name: pkt.pl
description: A Polish business database operated by WeNet Group S.A. Its single form covers both adding a company and updating an existing entry, and adding is free. The form requires JavaScript.
bestFor: Polish businesses wanting a second national directory entry alongside Panorama Firm.
Correcting company data already held in the database, which the same form covers.
notRecommendedFor: Anyone expecting a submission here to also reach Panorama Firm. Both are WeNet properties, but neither states that an entry reaches the other.
Users without JavaScript. The submission form states that it is required.
pros: The operating company is named directly in the form’s consent text — WeNet Group S.A. and WeNet Sp. z o.o. — which is unusually explicit for a directory.
One route covers both cases: the page is titled “Chcesz dodać lub aktualizować dane firmy na pkt.pl?”, so correcting existing data does not require a different journey.
Adding a company is free and stated as such: “Dodaj firmę bezpłatnie”.
The database indexes opinions alongside addresses and telephone numbers.
cons: The form covers updating an existing entry, but updating data is not the same as taking ownership of a profile, so no claim flow is asserted.
The submission form requires JavaScript and says so, which makes it unusable without a scripted browser.
The operator promotes better Google positioning as a benefit of listing. That is the operator’s marketing claim, and no ranking, indexing or traffic outcome is asserted by this record.
Nothing about verification is documented, so it is not asserted.
Opinions appear in the database, but whether a business can respond to them is not documented and is not asserted.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 from the database and its own submission page, and re-verified in a separate direct pass in which “dodać lub aktualizować dane firmy”, “WeNet Group S.A.” and “Dodaj firmę bezpłatnie” were each present in the served pages. PLATFORM OPERATOR: WeNet Group S.A., named directly in the submission form’s consent text alongside WeNet Sp. z o.o. LISTING CONTROL: A business adds or updates its own data through one form. MODERATION AUTHORITY: Not documented by the operator. PUBLIC INTERFACE: pkt.pl, with the add-or-update form at /dodaj-aktualizuj-dane-firmy. DUPLICATE DECISION: kept separate from Panorama Firm despite shared WeNet group ownership. Different domains, different submission forms, and pkt.pl carries its own site terms. Ownership is not evidence that businesses manage one shared profile, and no operator states that a submission reaches both. MARKETING CLAIM NOT ADOPTED: the submission page promotes “Wyższa pozycja w Google”. That is promotional copy, not documentation, and no SEO outcome is asserted anywhere in this record. NOT ASSERTED: verification, owner responses, claim flow, indexability, link attributes, traffic.

name: Firmy.net
description: A Polish business directory operated by NNV Sp. z o.o. since 2007. A company presentation is created free of charge after registering an account, and the operator states that entries are also distributed to partner portals — which is useful to know before submitting.
bestFor: Polish businesses wanting a free company presentation with a named, long-established operator.
Businesses that want one submission to reach partner portals as well as the directory itself.
notRecommendedFor: Businesses that want their entry confined to one site. The operator states it is distributed to partner portals.
Anyone expecting the search-position claims on the signup page to be guaranteed. They are marketing, not commitments.
pros: Creating a presentation is free and the operator says so twice over: “Rozpocznij darmową reklamę Twojej firmy!” and “Zarejestruj się i promuj firmę bezpłatnie”.
The operator is identified in both the footer and the signup form’s data-protection notice: “Administratorem danych osobowych jest NNV Sp. z o.o.”
The operating history is long and stated on the site, running from 2007.
The submission is a genuine self-service route with its own page, not an enquiry form.
cons: Your entry does not stay on this site alone. The operator states a presentation reaches customers “z Google, aplikacji mobilnych oraz kilkunastu portali partnerskich” — from Google, mobile apps and more than a dozen partner portals. Where those entries appear is not enumerated.

The signup page claims a presentation “natychmiast po utworzeniu osiąga wysokie pozycje w wynikach wyszukiwania” — that it immediately reaches high positions in search results. That is the operator’s marketing claim and is NOT adopted here; no ranking outcome is asserted.
An account with a confirmed email address is required before a presentation exists, so this is not an anonymous submission.
Creating a presentation is documented; claiming an existing third-party entry is not, so no claim flow is asserted.
Whether verification is required, and by what method, is not documented, so nothing about verification is asserted.
No review system or owner-response function is documented, so neither is asserted.
No Domain Rating is published for this platform. No valid measurement exists in the frozen historical set and none may be estimated, so the metric is recorded as not measured rather than guessed.
A listing is a directory entry. It is not evidence that a business is solvent, currently trading, licensed, or checked beyond what the operator documents here.
No ranking, indexing, traffic or lead outcome is asserted. The operator markets outcomes; this record does not adopt them.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 from the platform’s own signup page and footer, and re-verified in a separate direct pass in which “NNV Sp. z o. o.”, “Rozpocznij darmową reklamę Twojej firmy!” and “kilkunastu portali partnerskich” were each present in the served pages. PLATFORM OPERATOR: NNV Sp. z o.o., named in the site footer and in the signup form’s data-protection notice.
